rule: R-19's blocking half, repo-wide: a standing adverse oracle verdict whose leaf a committed baseline holds a different value than is a baseline pinned over a dissent, which the R-15/R-18 amendment names as the campaign's own failure shape. Every member of that population owes a row here. A row is one of two kinds and there is no third, because 'we looked at it' is not an adjudication: a CITATION says no oracle was ever owed and names the ruling that decides the leaf; an OPEN_DEBT says one was, names what is owed under the amendment's two clauses, and names the artifact carrying it.
what_this_file_does_not_do: It decides no dissent. Clearing one is a fresh whole-series re-adjudication or a ruled src/ correction, and neither is a scan's or a lane's to perform. What it removes is the population's ability to grow in silence: scripts/standing_dissent_scan.py --check fails on a member with no row, on a row whose dissent has cleared, and therefore on any future capture that pins over a standing verdict.

measured_on_the_commit_that_lands_this.what_moved_it: The docketed re-adjudication filed 21 receipts. 19 dissents cleared by supersession and their rows moved to cleared[]; 2 of the filed receipts returned `both_wrong` and are standing dissents in their own right, so they gained rows. The blocking population fell 28 -> 11 and the open debts 22 -> 5, without a baseline moving in either direction. Then Amendment J landed and the coverage-prose row stopped being a debt: it is a citation to the ruling that decides the leaf, so the citations read 7 and the open debts 4. The standing and blocking counts do not move with it -- the dissent still stands and the baseline still holds the other string, which is exactly what a citation row is for: it says no oracle was ever owed on this clause, not that the oracle was wrong. Moved again the same day by the DKT ruling's nine filed verdicts: oracle_receipts 573 -> 582 and nothing else. All nine returned new_value_correct, so adverse_verdicts, standing, blocking and by_kind are unchanged -- and none of the nine clears a standing dissent either, because no leaf address any of them adjudicates is one a standing member holds (checked normalized for the leading slash, which 189 of the 582 receipts omit). Moved once more, still the same day, by the RW-scenarios pass's six filed verdicts on the deferral-coverage capture: oracle_receipts 582 -> 588 and nothing else. All six returned new_value_correct, so adverse_verdicts, standing, blocking and by_kind are again unchanged, and none of the six clears a standing dissent -- two adjudicate coupled-scenario memberships no standing member's leaf address touches, and the other four adjudicate the snapshot's own shape counters, which no dissent in this file is filed on (checked normalized for the leading slash, as above). Moved a fifth time on 2026-08-16 by the RW-window-scenarios pass's six filed verdicts on the window-armed coverage capture: oracle_receipts 588 -> 594 and nothing else. All six returned new_value_correct, so adverse_verdicts, standing, blocking and by_kind are unchanged again, and none of the six clears a standing dissent -- the same two shapes as the pass before it, two coupled-scenario memberships (lethality_window_assassin_roster, liandry_reprice_mage_roster) and four shape counters, and no standing member holds any of those six addresses (checked normalized for the leading slash, which 189 of the 594 receipts omit). Moved a sixth time on 2026-08-17 by the RW-swing-scenarios pass's three filed verdicts on the swing-term coverage capture: oracle_receipts 594 -> 597 and nothing else. All three returned new_value_correct, so adverse_verdicts, standing, blocking and by_kind are unchanged again, and none of the three clears a standing dissent -- the same two shapes as the two passes before it, one coupled-scenario membership (swing_term_armed_carry_roster) and two shape counters, and no standing member holds any of those three addresses (checked normalized for the leading slash, which 189 of the 597 receipts omit). The pass is smaller than the two before it because it filed one verdict per qualifying occurrence its capture's allowlist declared -- three, not the five-member population -- so a shrinking pass here is the declaration being followed rather than coverage being lost.

adjudications.what_is_owed: Clause 2, and not clause 1 again. The docketed re-adjudication of the cast-timeline cluster has run, and this receipt is its whole-series verdict on the address: it certifies neither side. 100.0 is Force of Will's rank-5 cost, which the corrected series holds one row later; the committed 0.0 prices a stocked Dark Sphere charge as free, which no MANA-resource charge ability in the cached roster is. What is owed is the producing correction re-opened -- C6's `recast_of="Q"` stamp as its own ruled src/ slice with its own `Expected qualifying occurrences` line -- and, until it lands, a committed baseline that does not absorb the leaf.
adjudications.why_it_is_a_debt_and_not_a_citation: A citation says no oracle was ever owed. One was owed here, was taken twice, and the second answer is a computation from the cached ability rows -- resource kind, cost modifiers, recharge rate, and the cross-champion survey of every charge ability in the cache. The transition is value-to-value on a leaf both sides hold, which is the one shape the R-15 amendment's citation route explicitly does not reach.

adjudications.cited_ruling: Amendment J — 2026-08-15, how a campaign-authored justification string is adjudicated (umbrella, criterion 5): a campaign-authored justification string that asserts a fact about src-level vocabulary is adjudicated BY SOURCE ASSERTION -- a machine check binding the string to the predicate that produces it -- and never by an R-18 investigation, whose export excludes src/ by design. The check is tests/test_coverage_reason_source_assertion.py: the sentence is emitted at exactly one site in src/, under `if declares_only_defence(name)`, and that predicate is `families <= _DEFENCE_FAMILIES` over the group RuleFamily itself declares, asserted over every cached item in both directions.
adjudications.the_declared_change: Phase 3's 3.8 coverage flip. The attacker ladder's rung 2 stopped being a name branch and became a declaration read -- `attacker.declared_defence_only`, keyed on item_coverage.declares_only_defence -- and the published receipt was reworded to say what the rung now reads: every declared family on this item is a defence. The leaf is that receipt string; no number moved with it, which is the same guard Amendment E's third clause states.
adjudications.why_no_oracle_could_answer_it: R-18's export is data/ plus docs/math-foundations.md and excludes src/ by design, and the disputed clause is a statement about src-level vocabulary: RuleFamily's defence group, which no cached artifact spells. The filed receipt says so about itself -- its limitations block records that a code-level family vocabulary, if one existed, was out of bounds for this runbook and was not consulted -- so its verdict is valid for the operative clause it certified on BOTH sides and does not reach the added universal. Under the ruling that portion is adjudicated by the source assertion instead, and the receipt stands exactly as filed rather than being re-run or re-graded.
adjudications.what_it_owed_until_the_ruling: A ruling on how a leaf whose value is a campaign-authored reason string is adjudicated at all. The R-19 verdict set has no member for 'the evidence tree cannot decide this', so an investigator handed a coverage reason must certify the old value.

The transition is value_to_absent/absent_to_value on a block the declared change created, and the ruling is one a reader can open.
adjudications.the_declared_change: D-72 and Phase 4 S9: the parallel `dispositions` map is a published block that did not exist when the baseline was captured, so `<absent> -> the map` is what the ruling says rather than a number anybody can price.
adjudications.why_no_oracle_could_answer_it: The receipt's own reasoning is the amendment's predicted failure reproduced verbatim: it grepped the R-18 export for 'disposition' and 'view_tag', found zero occurrences, and concluded the block should not exist. An investigator handed absent_to_value must still return a member of R-19's three-way set, so it certifies the old value, and a dissent meaning 'no evidence exists' is indistinguishable in a tally from one meaning 'the tree is wrong'.

how_a_row_leaves_this_file: A row leaves adjudications[] the moment its dissent stops blocking, and that moment is not a judgement: it is scripts/standing_dissent_scan.py's own `stale_rows` check, which is red on a row whose dissent has cleared. It lands in cleared[] rather than being deleted, because deleting it would cut the join between a debt and the receipt that discharged it, and that receipt is the only evidence the debt was paid rather than dropped. Each cleared row keeps its kind, its address and what it said was owed, verbatim, and adds the answer: the superseding receipt, its verdict, and the mechanism -- a same-leaf `new_value_correct` receipt not dated earlier than the dissent, which is the supersession rule the scan computes and no reader restates.

cleared.what_is_owed: The same two clauses, over the support-damage-multiplier series. The leaf the oracle certified a value for is absent from the committed baseline, which is the absorption in the other direction: the baseline dropped the number the oracle said was right.
cleared.why_it_is_a_debt_and_not_a_citation: The certified value is a priced multiplier with a sourced derivation from data/items.json, so it is exactly the question an oracle can answer and did.
cleared.mechanism: R-19 supersession as the scan computes it: the superseding receipt adjudicates the same leaf address, carries `new_value_correct`, and is dated no earlier than this dissent. No baseline moved -- the verdict certifies the value the committed coupled baseline already holds, so the leaf leaves the blocking population by being answered rather than by being absorbed.
